docs.title: steer-materials
docs.text:
Material definitions for the STEER simulation framework.

steer-materials provides base classes for representing physical materials — metals, solvents, and other substances — with built-in unit conversion, validation, and cost tracking.

It is a support package within the broader STEER (Storage Technology for Energy and Economic Research) ecosystem.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Validated properties — density, cost, and names are type-checked on assignment.
  • Automatic unit conversion — values are stored in SI internally and exposed in common units (g/cm³, $/kg).
  • Cost tracking — optional volume/mass tracking with automatic cost derivation.
  • Soft & hard ranges — each physical property carries a plausible range and an absolute bound.
  • Serialization — built-in JSON serialization via steer-core mixins.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
from steer_materials.Base import Metal

aluminum = Metal(
    name="Aluminum",
    density=2.7,        # g/cm³
    specific_cost=2.50, # $/kg
    color="silver",
)
print(aluminum.density)        # 2.7
print(aluminum.specific_cost)  # 2.5

docs.title: Metal
docs.text:
Metal(name: str, density: float, specific_cost: float, color: str)

Bases: _Material

A metallic material (e.g. aluminum, steel, copper).

Inherits all behavior from _Material. Use this class for metals used in cell enclosures, current collectors, and structural components.

Examples:

from steer_materials.Base import Metal

aluminum = Metal(
    name="Aluminum",
    density=2.7,        # g/cm³
    specific_cost=2.50, # $/kg
    color="silver",
)

git clone https://github.com/stanford-developers/steer-materials.git
cd steer-materials
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Internal unit convention
docs.text:
All values are stored internally in SI base units (kg, m) and converted to user-facing units (g/cm³, $/kg, g, cm³) in property getters. The conversion constants come from steer_core.Constants.Units:

Constant Value Meaning KG_TO_G 1000 kg → g G_TO_KG 0.001 g → kg M_TO_CM 100 m → cm CM_TO_M 0.01 cm → m

docs.title: Class hierarchy
docs.text:
• _Material — Base class providing name, density, specific_cost, color, and last_updated. Not instantiated directly.
  • Metal / Solvent — Concrete subclasses of _Material for different material categories.
  • _VolumedMaterialMixin — Mixin that adds volume, mass, and cost tracking. Combined with a _Material subclass via multiple inheritance.

docs.title: Mixins from steer-core
docs.text:
_Material inherits from four steer-core mixins:

Mixin Purpose ValidationMixin Type and range checking (validate_positive_float, validate_string) PropagationMixin Cascading updates when properties change DunderMixin __repr__, __eq__, and other dunder methods SerializerMixin JSON serialization and deserialization

docs.title: Tracking volume, mass, and cost
docs.text:
The _VolumedMaterialMixin adds optional volume/mass tracking with automatic cost derivation. To use it, create a combined class:

from steer_materials.Base import Metal, _VolumedMaterialMixin


class VolumedMetal(_VolumedMaterialMixin, Metal):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

docs.title: Initialize with volume
docs.text:
Provide volume in cm³ — mass and cost are computed automatically:

al = VolumedMetal(
    name="Aluminum",
    density=2.7,
    specific_cost=2.50,
    color="silver",
    volume=100.0,  # cm³
)

print(al.volume)  # 100.0  cm³
print(al.mass)    # 270.0  g
print(al.cost)    # 0.68   $

docs.title: Initialize with mass
docs.text:
Provide mass in grams instead — volume is back-calculated:

al = VolumedMetal(
    name="Aluminum",
    density=2.7,
    specific_cost=2.50,
    color="silver",
    mass=270.0,  # g
)

print(al.volume)  # 100.0  cm³

docs.title: Omit both
docs.text:
If neither volume nor mass is given, all three remain None until assigned:

al = VolumedMetal(
    name="Aluminum", density=2.7, specific_cost=2.50, color="silver"
)
print(al.volume)  # None
print(al.mass)    # None
print(al.cost)    # None

al.volume = 50.0
print(al.mass)  # 135.0 g
print(al.cost)  # 0.34  $

Mutual exclusivity

You cannot provide both volume and mass at the same time:

# Raises ValueError
VolumedMetal(
    name="Al", density=2.7, specific_cost=2.50, color="silver",
    volume=100.0, mass=270.0,
)

docs.title: Propagation on property changes
docs.text:
When you update density or specific_cost, derived values recalculate automatically:

al = VolumedMetal(
    name="Aluminum", density=2.7, specific_cost=2.50,
    color="silver", volume=100.0,
)

# Change density — mass and cost update, volume stays
al.density = 5.0
print(al.volume)  # 100.0
print(al.mass)    # 500.0
print(al.cost)    # 1.25

# Change specific cost — cost updates, mass stays
al.specific_cost = 5.0
print(al.mass)  # 500.0
print(al.cost)  # 2.5

docs.title: Clearing volume/mass
docs.text:
Set volume or mass to None to clear all derived values:

al.volume = None
print(al.volume)  # None
print(al.mass)    # None
print(al.cost)    # None

docs.title: Comparing materials
docs.text:
Materials provide a human-readable representation via steer-core mixins:

copper = Metal(name="Copper", density=8.96, specific_cost=8.00, color="orange")
print(copper)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide walks you through creating materials with steer-materials.

docs.title: Creating a Metal
docs.text:
from steer_materials.Base import Metal

steel = Metal(
    name="Steel",
    density=7.87,       # g/cm³
    specific_cost=0.80, # $/kg
    color="grey",
)

All inputs are validated on construction — passing a negative density or a non-string name raises immediately:

# This raises ValueError:
Metal(name="Bad", density=-1.0, specific_cost=1.0, color="red")

# This raises TypeError:
Metal(name=123, density=7.87, specific_cost=0.80, color="grey")

docs.title: Creating a Solvent
docs.text:
from steer_materials.Base import Solvent

water = Solvent(
    name="Water",
    density=1.0,
    specific_cost=0.01,
    color="clear",
)

docs.title: Reading properties
docs.text:
Properties are returned in user-friendly units:

print(steel.density)         # 7.87  (g/cm³)
print(steel.specific_cost)   # 0.80  ($/kg)
print(steel.name)            # "Steel"
print(steel.last_updated)    # "2026-03-17 10:30:00"

docs.title: Updating properties
docs.text:
Setters validate input and trigger dependent recalculations:

steel.density = 8.0
print(steel.density)  # 8.0

steel.name = "Stainless Steel"

docs.title: Inspecting ranges
docs.text:
Each property has a soft range (±10 % for density, 0.5×–2× for cost) and a hard range (absolute bounds):

print(steel.density_range)       # (7.08, 8.66)
print(steel.density_hard_range)  # (0, 100)
